result.rationale: The diff shows TopicRetriever#invalid_host? only validates URI(@embed_url).host against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, then fetches via TopicEmbed.import_remote's `open(url).read`. Ruby's Kernel#open (open-uri) follows HTTP redirects, so a URL on the whitelisted host that redirects elsewhere bypasses the host check, and the fetched HTML is imported raw (cook_method raw_html) and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb — a real SSRF/redirect-bypass path introduced by this diff. Mechanism is grounded in the diff; severity depends on external redirect behavior, so confidence is moderate.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, the only constraint is `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`, which validates only the original URL’s host. But `TopicEmbed.import_remote` then does `open(url).read` (open-uri) which will follow HTTP redirects by default. Therefore a URL on the allowed `embeddable_host` that 30x-redirects to another host can cause Discourse to fetch and import content from an attacker-controlled destination, bypassing the intended host restriction shown in this diff.
